digest.component_or_area: store lock ownership and timeout messaging
propositions: A blocked writer encountering a store lock timeout receives only a bare pid of the holder, not the holder's operation type, making it unsafe to interrupt without manual investigation
Compaction sweeps are interruptible (skipped sweeps are no-ops and the next trigger re-folds events), but operators cannot determine this from timeout messages alone
The holder's operation context is already known at lock acquisition time but does not reach the timeout message

An ambient contextvar-based operation label mechanism can propagate the holder's operation type through the lock acquisition path to the owner stamp without modifying per-ticket acquisition call sites
The lock timestamp format must remain colon-free for backward compatibility while adding an optional sanitized op=label field that is ignored by staleness logic
The LockTimeout message should include a remedy line for known interruptible operations like compaction sweeps, indicating the holder can be safely interrupted and data will not be lost
